learning_outcomes.text: Ability to write and develop projects in the field of industrial engineering aimed at the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly or operation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical and electronic installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing and automation processes.
Ability to manage the activities that are the object of the engineering projects described in the previous section.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity and critical reasoning.
Ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and aptitudes in the field of Industrial Engineering, both orally and in writing, and to all types of audiences.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding, and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Ability to know, select, criticize, and use diverse sources of information.
Ability to work in a team.
Knowledge of applied thermodynamics and heat transfer. Basic principles and their application to solving engineering problems.
Knowledge of the basic principles of fluid mechanics and their application to solving problems in the field of engineering. Calculation of pipes, channels and fluid systems.
Knowledge and skills to organize and manage projects. Understanding the organizational structure and functions of a project office.
Analyze the social and technological potential of renewable energy sources, identifying their real advantages and disadvantages.
Understand the fundamentals of energy technologies that utilize renewable energy sources.
Know and propose more energy-efficient installations.
Assess the energy recovery potential of various waste or residual energies.
Prepare the preliminary project of an energy installation that uses a renewable energy source.

syllabus_topics: Contexto social y tecnológico de las energías renovables. Eficiencia energética. Régimen de subvenciones. Criterios de eficiencia en plantas de poligeneración. Tecnologías de cogeneración: turbinas de vapor, turbinas y microturbinas de gas, motores de combustión interna, pilas de combustible. Trigeneración.
Valoración energética de corrientes residuales. Ciclo Kalina. Ciclo Rankine Orgánico. Bomba de calor mecánica y de absorción. Recuperadores de calor.
Utilización de la biomasa y energía geotérmica

Recursos de la biomasa: biomasa natural, biomasa residual, cultivos energéticos y biocarburantes. Plantas de aprovechamiento de biomasa sólida. Energía geotérmica. Tipos y aplicaciones. Ciclos binarios. Sistemas de muy baja temperatura.

Astronomía de posición solar. Radiación solar extraterrestre. Interacción atmosférica: Componentes directa y difusa. Climatología. Radiación solar sobre superficies horizontales. Radiación solar sobre superficies inclinadas. Pérdidas de radiación.

Sistemas activos y pasivos. Captador de placa plana. Orientación, inclinación, distribución y conexionado de los captadores. Necesidad de acumulación en sistemas activos. Esquemas básicos de sistemas activos. Energía auxiliar. Elementos accesorios. Seguridad intrínseca contra sobrecalentamientos. Cálculo de cargas térmicas en instalaciones. Fracción de cobertura solar y rendimiento de instalaciones. Tubos de vacío y tubos de calor. Aplicaciones termosolares a medias y bajas temperaturas. Concentradores solares. Seguimiento solar. Aplicaciones termosolares a altas temperaturas. Centrales solares de ciclo Rankine. Sistemas Dish-Stirling. El hidrógeno como vector energético.

Electrónica básica de semiconductores. Estructura de una célula solar. Corriente de oscuridad. Eficiencia cuántica y corriente de cortocircuito. Característica ideal de una célula solar. Rendimiento. Influencia de la temperatura. Influencia de la concentración óptica. Tipos de células fotovoltaicas. El módulo fotovoltaico. Acumuladores, reguladores e inversores. Dimensionado de instalaciones fotovoltaicas. Introducción a la optimización de instalaciones fotovoltaicas.

Recursos hidráulicos, tipos de centrales hidráulicas y elementos principales. Nociones de hidrología: precipitaciones, filtración, evaporación y escorrentía. Estimación del potencial hidráulico. Turbinas hidráulicas: velocidad específica, tipos principales y regulación. Presas, conducciones, aliviaderos y otros elementos hidráulicos de centrales.
Características del viento y potencial eólico. Tipos de aerogeneradores. Parques eólicos.
Energía mareomotriz. Energía de corrientes. Energía undimotriz. Aprovechamiento de los gradientes térmico y salino.
Estudio técnico, económico y medioambiental de una instalación energética con fuentes de energía renovable (cogeneración, biomasa, geotermia)
teaching_methods: Virtual Campus activities (reading theoretical foundations, completing questionnaires, participating in debate forums, viewing additional material)

assessment_methods.method: Participation in the classroom (PA): exercises, practice reports, seminars, individual or group work, and oral presentations
Written exam (EX): questions and exercises from course content, divided into three blocks

assessment_rules: For students with continuous assessment, the final grade (NOTA) is calculated as (0.6 x PA) + (0.4 x EX), provided EX is 3 or higher and participation (PA) is at least 75%. Otherwise, the NOTA is capped at 4.9. To pass, the course grade must be 5.0 or higher. For students with differentiated assessment, the NOTA is solely the EX grade, which must be 5.0 or higher to pass. Extraordinary calls for both types of students consist of a single written exam (EX), which must be 5.0 or higher to pass.
